label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
changed_since_round_1: Better: the cover now carries a promise line, the 3-page edition lost a page, the five steps in the long edition now end the book, the three accounts of the 95% are in the body, the researcher's finding now names its claim, and the editions say a newsroom could use it. Worse: the long edition's picture slots are now labelled 'Figure to come' in dashed boxes, which still reads as a draft, and the editor's decision is still not stated. Unchanged: most pages are half to two thirds empty and the source lines are still file paths.

round_1_changes_done.change: Remove the review stamp from the running head
Fill the cover with a promise line
Draw the pictures or remove the bracketed stage directions
Say what the argument was and what the signature decided
Put the three accounts of the 95% in the body
Name the claim the researcher checked
Fold the contents page into the cover or an opener
Set 'Where this came from' in plain words, not repository paths
Say which role to hire first

03.one_line: Four pages of voices and one boxed list of four steps, with the 18:44 stop and a named row of what it costs, make a clear first day for a newsroom, but the cover is still mostly white and the editor's signature is never named as the control.

10.one_line: The reviewer line, the researcher's objection withdrawn, the three accounts of the stop and the five steps on page 10 are the record I trust, but three dashed 'Figure to come' boxes and half-empty pages make it look unfinished.

the_page: Type is comfortable on a laptop: a heavy sans headline, a serif body, a rust rule and a cast bar on every page, and each page holds one idea, which is a real strength. The only graphic devices are the grey word boxes and the numbered step boxes, and the dashed figure placeholders on 10-page pages 2, 3, 7 and 8 crowd the text with an empty promise rather than help it. Pages 4 to 9 of the long edition and page 5 of the short one are over half blank, and the margins still shift left and right from page to page.

best_page.why: Five numbered steps, one action each, a newsroom named as a use ('a newsroom's daily stories'), a cost line that admits the day's own cost is not in the record, and a pointer on. I can act on it in five minutes.

worst_page.why: The failures page, the part I trust most, opens with a dashed empty box and then holds five short lines, leaving over half the page blank; it feels like a slip, and the lines do not say which checks missed or what the claims were.

changes.quote: Figure to come: the cast cards for the four
changes.change: Draw the cast cards and the strips on pages 2, 7 and 8, or delete the dashed boxes from the reader's copy.
changes.why: A box that says 'to come' reads as a draft and makes the page look like something broke.

changes.quote: I kept the line. The book keeps the argument.
changes.change: Say in one plain sentence what the line was and what the editor's signature decided, in both editions (10-page edition page 6 too).
changes.why: My deal-breaker is an editor who only rubber-stamps; the page shows a decision but not its content, so I cannot tell a control from a ritual.

changes.quote: The checks worked, and they also missed.
changes.change: Name one miss and what it cost, as the researcher's claim was named on page 6.
changes.why: The sourced failure is the proof; an unnamed miss is an assertion.

changes.change: Say which role a newsroom hires first (the researcher, with a reviewer) and why, in the step list or a line under it.
changes.why: The editions still never say which role to start with, and it is my first question.

changes.change: Put the nine-agent cast as a row of initials and the date on the cover, and move the title block up.
changes.why: Two thirds of the cover is white, and the cover must make me want to start.

changes.change: Replace repository paths with plain-words sources (the talk's register, the agents' own debriefs) and put the paths online.
changes.why: A reader cannot trace an internal file name; it is the book's trust signal and it is unreadable.

changes.quote: Reviewer (a second agent with a checker's brief, drawn as a clipboard)
changes.change: Cut the stage direction 'drawn as a clipboard' from the printed line, or draw it, and fill the empty lower half with the first review's exact output.
changes.why: The strongest idea of the book (a second reading, not a second identity) sits on a page that is 60 per cent blank, with a picture that is only described.

changes.change: Fix the text block margins so they do not jump between pages 2, 3 and 4 and beyond, and merge pages 8 and 9 or lift the closing pages to fill them.
changes.why: The shifting left edge looks like a layout fault on a laptop and the half-empty pages undo the calm.

notes: The voices are still the best thing: the tags such as '(unbudging)' and '(exacting, to ruv-sgit)' carry the cast with no picture needed. The 3-page edition feels more finished than the 10-page one because it has no empty figure boxes. No religious words found.
